nodes.description: OER performance evaluation of equiatomic Ni-Pd-Pt-Ru library using scanning droplet cell measurements
nodes.source_text: Figure 3a exemplarily shows the LSVs obtained from SDC measurements of the equiatomic materials library, color-coded by their current density at a potential of 1.7 V versus RHE, and the resulting activity distribution on ML1. The activity in this library increases with higher Ru-contents. Figure 3b combines compositional data with measured activities, forming the training dataset for the Bayesian optimization algorithm. The highest measured activity of 1.65 mAcm⁻² was found in the Ru-rich library within the high Ru content region.

nodes.source_text: Figure 5a shows the compositional distribution and corresponding electrochemical activity of ML6. The binary composition spread exhibits a gradient with high Ru content in the top right and high Ni content in the bottom left of the library, resulting in an activity distribution symmetric along the diagonal. As expected, higher Ru contents correlate with increased activity. The activities measured in ML6 surpass those of all previously tested compositions, and the observed trend indicates a global activity maximum at pure Ru. In the Ru-rich regions of ML7 and ML9, particularly in the Ru-rich library (ML3) and the binary Ni-Ru library (ML6), the crystal structure transitions into hexagonal closed packed (hcp) as the dominant phase.

nodes.description: OER performance at fixed potential 1.6 V vs RHE for cost-activity trade-off analysis

analysis_purpose.value: Pareto front analysis for cost-activity trade-off

cost_efficiency.value: highest cost among elements but best activity

nodes.source_text: The current density at 1.6 V versus RHE was chosen as an activity measure in order to avoid the plateau of the LSVs in the Ru-rich areas likely caused due to mass transport limitations and bubble formation during the measurement. The Pareto front spans between pure Ru and pure Ni and highlights the steep increase in activity with higher Ru-content on ML6.

nodes.characterization_summary: Linear sweep voltammetry obtained via scanning droplet cell (SDC) measurements to determine electrochemical activity. Current density at 1.7 V versus RHE extracted as activity measure. Pure Ru exhibits highest activity with rapid increase in current density peaking just below 1.7 V versus RHE; Ni shows moderate activity; Pd and Pt exhibit lowest OER activity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical screening, performed using a scanning droplet cell (SDC) setup, requires the longest time... the current densities at a potential of 1.7 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) were extracted from the LSVs... Among the four elements, pure Ru exhibits the highest activity characterized by a rapid increase in current density, peaking just below 1.7 V versus RHE. Ni shows moderate activity, with a less steep yet noticeable rise in current density at higher potentials, while Pd and Pt exhibit the lowest OER activity.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy could provide insights into surface composition but was not performed in this study due to impractical measurement and analysis time for entire materials libraries.
nodes.evidence_snippet: While X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) could provide insights into the surface composition, its measurement and analysis time remains significantly longer than other high-throughput techniques like EDX, making it impractical for measuring entire materials libraries.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical surface area measurements were not performed but are suggested as a potential high-throughput technique to address the influence of morphology on catalytic activity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Similarly, incorporating high-throughput electrochemical surface area (ECSA) measurements could address the influence of morphology by weighting the activity appropriately.
